transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?
Thank you for seeing me. I’ve started having these beliefs that something is going on behind the scenes at work, and even when people tell me it’s not true, I just can’t shake the feeling.
How long have you been having these beliefs—has it been less than a month, between one and six months, or longer than six months?
It’s definitely been longer than six months. These beliefs started after I got back from a trip about a year and a half ago, and they've been pretty constant for the last year and a few months.
Have you noticed any hallucinations, like hearing voices or seeing things that other people do not, or is it mainly the fixed belief that people are plotting or acting behind the scenes?

Yes, I actually do hear a low male voice pretty often when I'm alone in my apartment, calmly commenting on what I'm doing and telling me "you messed that up" when I'm checking sales numbers. On top of that, I still can't shake the feeling that my managers and coworkers are running some kind of secret test on me by purposely changing my table sections or ticket times.

Besides the voice and the belief that coworkers are testing you, have you noticed any other changes such as disorganized thinking or speech, strange behavior, or a decline in your work or daily functioning?

Yes, my brain constantly feels foggy and overloaded, making it hard to read simple order tickets or make basic choices. Because of this, my performance at work has really slipped, and I've even been written up for slower ticket times and missed shifts. Outside of work, I've been avoiding my family and letting my apartment get completely messy because I just can't keep up with basic chores anymore.
Have you noticed a reduced ability to feel pleasure or interest in things you used to enjoy, or feeling emotionally flat or detached from other people?

Yes, I've completely lost interest in things I used to love and feel totally flat emotionally. On my days off, instead of cooking new recipes or meeting up with friends, I just sit on the couch staring at my notebooks. I just can't bring myself to get moving or feel anything anymore.
Have you also noticed any odd or disorganized speech or behavior, like others saying your thoughts are hard to follow, or you acting in a way that seems very unusual to people around you?

I don't think my speech has been hard to follow, and no one has mentioned me acting in a highly unusual or disorganized way. They have, however, noticed that I've become very quiet and seem really slowed down lately.
Have you had any periods where your mood was very depressed or very elevated, or where the voices and beliefs only happened during a mood episode?

Most days I feel incredibly depressed and empty, though I've never had any times where my mood felt elevated or high. Usually, the voice and the paranoia happen right along with my low mood, but there was a two-week stretch late last summer where my mood and energy briefly improved while the voice and beliefs stayed just as strong.
Have there been any periods of at least 2 weeks when you had hallucinations or paranoid beliefs even though your mood was not depressed or elevated at all?

Yes, late last summer there was a stretch of at least two weeks where my mood and energy picked up and I didn't feel as depressed. But even during that time, I still clearly heard the voice in my apartment and remained convinced that my coworkers were running those experiments on me.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when the hallucinations or paranoid beliefs were present even though you were not feeling depressed or unusually elevated at all?

Yes, like I mentioned, that happened late last summer for about two weeks. My mood actually felt okay and my energy was up, but the voice and the feeling that my coworkers were testing me didn't go away at all.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when you had the voice or the paranoid beliefs even though you were not feeling depressed, empty, or unusually high at all?

Yes, that's exactly what happened during those two weeks late last summer. Even though I wasn't feeling depressed or empty during that brief stretch, the voice in my apartment and the belief that my coworkers were testing me stayed completely the same.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a chronic psychotic illness with persistent auditory hallucinations, fixed persecutory delusions, negative symptoms (flat affect, avolition/anhedonia, social withdrawal), and marked functional decline. Psychotic symptoms have been present for over 6 months and clearly occurred for at least 2 weeks in the absence of a mood episode, supporting schizophrenia rather than a mood disorder with psychotic features or delusional disorder.
